Capability.meaning: Explicit operation grant on a resource or permission scope.

PrincipalGroup.meaning: Direct membership in a configured role or user group; a group can itself be a member. Supplied by trusted configuration or an authoritative identity source, never inferred from an agent-chosen name.

ResourceGroup.meaning: Permission-scope membership; grants on a parent apply to its descendants.

InGroup.meaning: Direct or nested role/user-group membership from PrincipalGroup. Membership alone is not permission.

Can.meaning: Grant including declared principal and resource memberships; not final authorization.

Field.meaning: Host-observed field or association of an application object or event. The binding defines cardinality, value type, fixed unit and optional observation-time field; never agent claims or hidden policy decisions.

Event.meaning: An event observed by the host, with its ID, actor and kind; recording it does not imply permission or success.

scope: Captured gate inputs and mediated callbacks. Outcomes follow the trusted adapter's confirmation contract; they are not independent proof of business success or authentic identity. Unmediated channels and missing observations remain outside this trace.

parameters.notes: Claim verification: the strongest claims are properly evidenced — the $20bn search payment is correctly attributed as a 2022 litigated estimate rather than an Apple disclosure (S70), the two-point tariff refund and $0.11 EPS come from the 30 July 2026 release (S17), the China share numbers reconcile Counterpoint (S139) against IDC (S140) including the 19.5% versus 17.8% difference, and the Ninth Circuit and Mehta remedies are dated and cited (S76, S79). Tested and holding: market value $613B x 1.0bn units x $581 ASP bottom-up, 36-43% value capture, 0.97x normalised conversion bridge, 6.05 weighted composite. Failed: the FY2026 consensus sentence. parameters.items: [{"action":"Add the adoption series that would evidence or kill the AI cycle: installed-base upgrade rate by cohort, iPhone unit growth implied by $196.5bn of nine-month revenue at the $941 ASP, switcher or churn data, and any Siri AI engagement disclosure. If units are not in the register, present the price-versus-unit decomposition explicitly rather than attributing 22.4% iPhone growth to Pro mix.","evidence_request":"What were iPhone units and the upgrade rate in 9M FY2026 versus 9M FY2025, and what share of the installed base has activated Siri AI since 2026-09-14?","issue":"The AI upgrade cycle carries the bull case, but there is no adoption evidence anywhere: no iPhone unit growth, no upgrade rate, no switcher or churn rate, no Siri AI activation or engagement figure. iPhone revenue of $196.5bn in nine months at a $941 implied ASP is read as mix, which is one of several explanations (price, mix, units) and is not separated from them.","sections":["technology_product","market","strategy","thesis"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Add a short section on how the customer pays after a 27.6% ASP rise: financing and installment penetration, the Klarna Apple Upgrade economics, carrier subsidy direction, and the India and enterprise channels. State what would show demand breaking on price.","evidence_request":"What share of iPhone sales is financed or on installment, how has that share moved with the 2026 price increases, and are carrier subsidies rising or falling?","issue":"The budget owner is stated as the consumer or carrier financing plan but never analysed, and the mechanism that makes a $1,199 phone affordable into a memory-led price rise is absent: no financing or installment penetration, no carrier subsidy trend, no Apple Upgrade or Klarna economics beyond a table entry, and no enterprise or education channel. Price elasticity is the central swing in the scenario table and the cheapest thing to test.","sections":["market","strategy","business_model"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"State that no lost-deal or return data is in the register and what that does to confidence in the competitive judgement.","evidence_request":"","issue":"No lost-deal evidence: the report never says why a buyer chose Samsung or Huawei in a specific case, and Duo return and durability data is marked not disclosed without a statement of the cost to the foldable case.","sections":["competition","technology_product"],"severity":"Minor"}]
parameters.notes: Product/market-fit pass. Hardest thing about selling, as the report implies but does not state: holding a $1,199-$1,299 price into a 27.6% ASP rise while a rival ships the same frontier model Apple licenses. Budget owner: consumer or carrier financing, correctly named but unquantified. Sales cycle: annual September launch, well described. Why adoption is not faster: unanswered for the AI feature (beta, English-only, no engagement data). Lost deals: absent. Questions a partner would ask: (1) how many of the 22.4% iPhone revenue growth points are price, mix and units? (2) what share of buyers finances the handset and at what monthly cost? (3) if Siri AI were a demand driver, what would the December quarter show? (4) what does a Duo return look like against a Pro Max? (5) which specific customer loss in China was attributable to Huawei rather than to market size?

parameters.items: [{"action":"Designate one governing method for the entry rule, show the margin of safety at $270 against it, and present the two bases as a range with the multiple method labelled a market-price cross-check. Stress terminal growth at 2.5-3.0% and show what that does to the $212.","evidence_request":"What terminal growth does the perpetual model need to reach $270, and at what discount rate does the sum of the parts reach the first tranche?","issue":"The actionable price contradicts the valuation. The first tranche of $270 is 27% above the report's own DCF value of $212 and 13% above the top of the sum of the parts ($238), and the bear DCF is $133, yet the entry is justified by a third method, 29x on FY2027 EPS, which yields $284. Executive summary and scoring then call $284 the base case and $212 the DCF, so a reader is given two base values and one entry price above both lower ones. Terminal growth of 4% is also generous for a business whose revenue compounded 3.3% a year in FY2021-25, and the sensitivity grid never tests below 3.0%, so the $212 is the optimistic end of its own method.","sections":["thesis","executive_summary","scoring","funding_valuation"],"severity":"Critical"},{"action":"Reconcile each figure to one number and one basis, and make the market-cap denominator (shares x price) explicit so every per-share output ties.","evidence_request":"","issue":"Key figures disagree across sections: market capitalisation $5,029.6bn (executive summary, valuation, exit) against $5,072bn (business model, financials); FY2025 buybacks $90.7bn against $89.3bn in strategy; TTM services gross margin 76.0% in valuation and market against 76.3% elsewhere; bear case $241 in the scenario table against $242 in thesis, exit and risk; the Gemini licence 0.6% of operating income in risk against 0.9% in thesis; trailing P/E 39.5x against 39.3x; sell trigger $380 in thesis against $440-441 in exit and thesis. 14.698bn shares at $344.63 is $5,065bn, so neither market-cap figure ties to the register.","sections":["financials","funding_valuation","business_model","strategy","thesis","exit"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Show the Kelly inputs (edge, variance, horizon) or drop the Kelly framing, and make the 3.9% result and the 2.5-3.0% second tranche consistent.","evidence_request":"","issue":"The position-sizing table is internally inconsistent: full Kelly at $270 is given as 39% of the fund and the fraction used as one tenth, 3.9%, but the staged plan puts the second tranche at 2.5-3.0% and the cap at 5%. A 39% full Kelly on a single equity with a -10% to +32% one-year spread is not credible, and no inputs are shown.","sections":["scoring"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Print FY2026E to FY2029E EPS and the dividend path in the table, or footnote the arithmetic, so the entry price can be checked without the underlying model.","evidence_request":"","issue":"The entry grid (three-year return by entry and exit multiple) is arithmetically sound when tested but hides its earnings path: FY2029E EPS of $11.45 implies 9.5% growth from trailing $8.72 against the 8.0% the same table states.","sections":["exit"],"severity":"Minor"}]
parameters.notes: Stress arithmetic checked: 200bp of gross margin on $466.8bn is $9.3bn, $0.52 of EPS, 6.0% of $8.72 (correct); 500bp is $1.31 (correct); losing the $20bn payment at a 17.3% tax rate is $1.12, 12.9% (correct); 10% of iPhone at 39.9% is $0.55 (correct); 30% revenue lower at the 43% incremental margin gives about $95bn of operating income and $5.4 of EPS (correct). FCF 30% worse: 0.7 x $125.1bn = $87.6bn, inside the stated $85.8-89.1bn band, covers the $82.2bn buyback, not $97.9bn of buybacks and dividends (correct, and it is stated). DCF rate sensitivity: each 50bp worth 15-18% (consistent with the grid: 8.5% to 9.5% at 4% growth, $229 to $193, is -16%).
